overview: Key ranges are split into Raft groups; leader handles writes; ranges split/merge and rebalance automatically; metadata in an etcd-like store.

estimation.assumption: Three replicas with read/write quorum sizes of two.
estimation.result: Acknowledged replica sets intersect in the healthy, non-sloppy case.
estimation.implication: Quorum overlap alone does not give linearizability with concurrent writes; choose causal reconciliation or consensus explicitly.

components.purpose: User-facing caller for distributed kv store.
components.rationale: Keep validation and durable state in services; retry only according to the API contract.

components.purpose: Distribute incoming connections across healthy instances for distributed kv store.
components.rationale: Health checks and routing policy support scale-out; connection-based systems need compatible session routing.

components.purpose: Route ordered key ranges to their Raft leader. Writes commit after a majority quorum; reads use leader leases or ReadIndex. Split hot ranges and retry stale routing metadata.
components.rationale: Keep request handlers stateless where possible; the datastore or a fenced owner enforces concurrency invariants.

components.purpose: Each range has three replicas and versioned committed log entries. A new leader repairs followers by log replication and snapshots.
components.rationale: Define the partition key and consistency requirements; conditional writes protect version and ownership checks.

components.purpose: Maintain range boundaries, leader epochs and replica membership; fence obsolete leaders.
components.rationale: Use a quorum and fencing; possession of an expired lease must never authorize a stale writer.

accessPatterns: GET by key; PUT with causal or expected-version context.
constraints: Replicate every key. Dynamo exposes concurrent siblings; Raft commits one version order per range.

apiDetails.purpose: Read the latest available key version.
apiDetails.rationale: Return causal context for Dynamo reconciliation, or a committed leader-read version for range consensus.

apiDetails.purpose: Write a new version of a key.
apiDetails.rationale: Acknowledge only after the required replica quorum; retry using the same operation ID or version precondition.

buildSteps.title: Clients
buildSteps.explanation: In Design, add Web Client and name it “Clients”. Place it in the leftmost caller/background lane. User-facing caller for distributed kv store. Keep validation and durable state in services; retry only according to the API contract. Apply the configuration below and add the listed connections once both ends exist.

buildSteps.title: LB
buildSteps.explanation: In Design, add Load Balancer and name it “LB”. Place it in column 2, row 1 of the HLD; its callers are Clients. Distribute incoming connections across healthy instances for distributed kv store. Health checks and routing policy support scale-out; connection-based systems need compatible session routing. Apply the configuration below and add the listed connections once both ends exist.

buildSteps.title: Range routers
buildSteps.explanation: In Design, add Service and name it “Range routers”. Place it in column 3, row 1 of the HLD; its callers are LB. Route ordered key ranges to their Raft leader. Writes commit after a majority quorum; reads use leader leases or ReadIndex. Split hot ranges and retry stale routing metadata. Keep request handlers stateless where possible; the datastore or a fenced owner enforces concurrency invariants. Apply the configuration below and add the listed connections once both ends exist.

buildSteps.title: Raft range replicas
buildSteps.explanation: In Design, add Key-Value Store and name it “Raft range replicas”. Place it in column 4, row 1 of the HLD; its callers are Range routers. Each range has three replicas and versioned committed log entries. A new leader repairs followers by log replication and snapshots. Define the partition key and consistency requirements; conditional writes protect version and ownership checks. Apply the configuration below and add the listed connections once both ends exist.

buildSteps.title: Range directory
buildSteps.explanation: In Design, add Coordination and name it “Range directory”. Place it in column 4, row 2 of the HLD; its callers are Range routers, Raft range replicas. Maintain range boundaries, leader epochs and replica membership; fence obsolete leaders. Use a quorum and fencing; possession of an expired lease must never authorize a stale writer. Apply the configuration below and add the listed connections once both ends exist.

steps.title: Clients → LB → Range routers → Range directory
steps.explanation: Resolve the key range and its current leader epoch.

steps.title: Range routers → Raft range replicas
steps.explanation: The range leader appends a versioned log entry and waits for a majority before ack.

steps.title: Raft range replicas → Range directory
steps.explanation: The range group updates its fenced leader metadata; an isolated minority cannot commit.

steps.title: Clients → LB → Range routers → Raft range replicas
steps.explanation: Retry with the same operation identity against the new leader; reads use ReadIndex or a valid leader lease.

failureCases.scenario: A replica or leader is unavailable
failureCases.handling: Dynamo can use hinted handoff and repair with explicit conflict semantics. Range consensus needs a reachable majority; elect a fenced leader and repair followers from the log.

alternatives: Use Dynamo-style replication when application conflict resolution and partition availability are acceptable. Use leader-per-range consensus for committed per-key order, accepting unavailable writes without a majority.
